policy: A candidate must have a distinct trigger/boundary before implementation.
Problem evidence may justify incubation but is not skill-effectiveness evidence.
A newly created skill starts incubating and remains UNPROVEN unless a post-creation behavioral record supports more.
Overlap with existing or later-wave skills must be narrowed before ADOPT/MODIFY.
No Wave A candidate may be marked stable during incubation.

problem_evidence: Phase 11 re-audit PR #26 found implicit CI guarantees around matrix parity, shell/runtime evidence, skip/soft-fail behavior, and critical-suite presence that required dedicated hardening.
PR #26 GitHub Actions run 36686190812 demonstrated the problem class on Windows and Ubuntu, but predates this candidate skill and therefore is not effectiveness evidence.
decisions.rename_reason: The original 'ci-cd-reliability' scope is too broad and would overlap Wave B release/rollback engineering. Narrowing to 'ci-pipeline-reliability' keeps ownership on pre-deployment workflow signal integrity.

owns: CI workflow trigger and permission correctness
flaky-test handling policy and reproducible CI diagnostics

overlap_review.testing-typescript-systems: Distinct: test skill designs tests; CI skill ensures pipeline execution/reporting of those tests remains trustworthy.
overlap_review.phase15-release-rollback-engineering: Separated by rename/scope: CI pipeline ends at trustworthy pre-deployment gates; release/rollback owns production promotion/recovery.
overlap_review.phase15-supply-chain-security: Distinct: CI pipeline may enforce a supplied security gate but does not own dependency/provenance security policy.

minimum_criteria: detects one OS leg or critical test silently omitted from a shared matrix
rejects continue-on-error/conditional skip on required validation gates
separates test failure from CI harness/configuration failure
does not expand into deployment rollback design

decisions.next_action: Retain as incubating. Do not promote until a controlled post-creation CI reliability case executes.
